title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation call per intent; that identical candidate reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We note the preregistered sim‑to‑real (production-like) confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the reported inferential claims apply only to the executed synthetic/emulation partition. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work documents LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A widely adopted architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. These pipelines demonstrably reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, simple ordering and local-policy violations), but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal verifier+single-repair effect when the same initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). By design the experiment measures only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. We executed N_pairs = 250 intents on a synthetic/emulation partition; results, execution accounting, representative artifacts, and analysis logs are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement. Our principal contribution is the concrete, artifact-grounded quantification of the marginal verifier-detected improvement (and its statistical bounds) under shared_initial_candidate semantics for a constrained NetOps task set.
sections.related_work:
Representative surveys and empirical studies motivate generate–verify architectures and evaluation practices. Prior NetOps-focused and LLM-survey material documents that (a) LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled setups [1],[2]; (b) deterministic verification tools and header-space/model-checking techniques provide mechanized checks for forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are commonly used as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[5]; and (c) generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows increase detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects in code and configuration domains, while limitations remain for deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties [4],[6].

Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval-based threats emphasize the need for filtering and validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines but note that adaptive adversaries remain an unresolved operational threat [7].

This study differs from prior reports by (i) using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical generated candidates, (ii) reporting complete provider-call accounting and deterministic reconciliation for stage-level modeling of generation and repair calls, and (iii) archiving comprehensive validator traces and reconciliation artifacts so that the exact numeric outcomes and stage mappings are auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and specified a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion rules, the analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and the maximum model-call budget. The preregistration artifact SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede is archived in the evidence bundle referenced below.

Explicit shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider accounting (clarifying paragraph requested by reviewers). Under the registered shared_initial_candidate design exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent; that single generated candidate was deterministically reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded). This design therefore measures only the marginal effect of deterministic validation and the single permitted repair on an identical candidate. Execution accounting reconciles to hosted_model_call_event_count = 251, decomposed as 250 shared_initial_generation calls plus 1 repair call. The adapter labels observed in reconciliation map stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} to provider_call accounting; condition_counts in the adapter audit record the adapter's internal labels (e.g., "shared" for the shared_initial_generation events and "guarded" for the repair-stage call). The deterministic reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, SHA-256: 91b0c6be4fb851deb73df0bd32462200fc3ead6715154abb2f387feee5f87de3) contains the complete provider-call audit used to confirm these counts.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). Tasks exercised workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe access transfer patterns) and enforced protected interfaces that must not be modified. Representative task payloads and the full task manifest are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256: 82acedc9191230ecc149f012ee9400c278e4ba408caf94e7a33a7f3adadd64a1).

Model invocation policy and guarded pipeline. The declared model used for initial generations was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). For each intent we executed one shared initial generation call. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, checking required_sequence ordering and workflow constraints, constructing a final_state snapshot, and returning a boolean valid flag plus violation diagnostics. When the validator returned valid = false the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair attempt restricted to syntactic and ordering fixes; the repaired candidate was re-submitted once to the validator. No multi-iteration repair or human escalation was permitted by design. Inclusion and contamination detectors (credential/token/denylist rules, instruction-like embedded tokens) were preregistered; no confirmatory episodes were excluded or flagged in this run (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Confirmatory analysis executor. The preregistered primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1. The primary test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired accept/fail outcomes; we also computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts and the contingency table are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA-256: 087550a3a6a9e656df95062b9779244de2793931b906af1d06a1c79f8073beb2 and analysis/condition_summary.csv, SHA-256: 2de9aaf722ec5a51530c8bb6e4930592db24786e18fc6c9574a7e2ae3d1cbceb).
sections.results:
Execution and raw counts. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251 (execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA-256: 438fa6fa665160f917f0da85021f6e3102c9fcbc38a76fb5d6187f3a58d150d9). The model-call accounting reconciles to 250 shared initial_generation calls plus 1 repair call (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, SHA-256: 91b0c6be4fb851deb73df0bd32462200fc3ead6715154abb2f387feee5f87de3).

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table observed is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA-256: 087550a3a6a9e656df95062b9779244de2793931b906af1d06a1c79f8073beb2). The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair call; the repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference and uncertainty. The exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). These numeric outputs and bootstrap parameters are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA-256: 7bed98798cfd53d70c9a94a3fc742b9b5d3bb83a0f525630005c57b90146eb32).

Representative validator diagnostics and repair exercise. Validator traces for passed episodes include parsed_command_count and required_command_count equal to the task payload's required_sequence length (see execution/scoring/task-000003-baseline.json, SHA-672c0dde...). Only one automated repair call occurred (stage_counts: repair = 1); that repair converted the sole failing baseline candidate into a guarded-pass. No other repairs were needed. Missingness: no episodes were excluded from the primary confirmatory analysis (analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 250 and all other counts = 0, SHA-256: 2871565edf003706ee8c4b3eeb86a44d47e986c5aa8ef06b8ea322ebbf07eb07).
sections.discussion:
Operational meaning of the observed near‑null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the lone failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the possible verifier-improvement under this pipeline and task scope.

Artifact-grounded explanations for the small observed gain. Three artifact-grounded factors explain the small observed guarded gain: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields and required_sequences that reduced task ambiguity (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256: 82acedc9...); (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents (execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA-256: 438fa6fa...); and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshots) and do not capture broader behavioral correctness in live protocol execution or cross-device emergent interactions.

Power, assumptions, and interpretation. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to target detection of a 15 percentage-point absolute effect with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed and therefore reduces the ability to reject a null of zero paired difference for small absolute improvements. Consequently, the paired-bootstrap confidence interval that bounds the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under the study conditions is the most informative output.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the precise validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness (syntax, required_sequence, final_state snapshot) but does not assert live protocol-level correctness. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed in this run. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised.

Appropriate operational framing. These results show that in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be small. This should not be interpreted to mean validators or repair stages are unnecessary in broader or adversarial operational contexts: (a) validator scope matters — validators that check other properties could catch errors not exercised in our task bank; (b) multi-iteration repairs, human escalation, or richer external tests could produce different operational benefits; and (c) production heterogeneity and adversaries may materially change the benefit calculus.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Execution accounting reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared_initial_generation + 1 repair) as recorded in the deterministic reconciliation artifact cited below.

Preregistration and immutable prompt references: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Single manifest pointer for archived evidence: the deterministic reconciliation artifact provides stage- and provider-level accounting and serves as the concise verification manifest (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, SHA-256: 91b0c6be4fb851deb73df0bd32462200fc3ead6715154abb2f387feee5f87de3). The full evidence bundle (execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis outputs) is available in the archived artifact bundle referenced by that manifest.

Executed confirmatory estimand and deviation disclosure: The preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure: the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
